<entry id="D01113">
<head-word>דָּרַס</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to tread, stamp</italic>.</definition>
<notes> B. Kam. II, 1 דָּרְסָה על וכ' if she trod upon a vessel. Y. Maasr. II, 49
<sup>d</sup> bot. והוא עתיד לדוֹרְסָן dates which he intends to stamp; a. fr.—בית הדּוֹרְסִין, v. מַעֲגִיל.—Part. pass. דָּרוּס, f. דְּרוּסָה.—דְּרוּסַת איש (calcata a viro) 
<italic>deflowered.</italic> Keth. I, 7.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition> (ritual) 
<italic>to press</italic>, i.e. 
<italic>to cut the throat of an animal by pressing the knife</italic> (adding muscular force to the cutting capacity of the knife, instead of passing the latter to and back).</definition>
<notes> Ḥull. 20
<sup>b</sup>. Ib. 30
<sup>b</sup> שמא יִדְרוֹסוּ זה על זה lest they press the knife by one adding to the strength of the other.—Denom. דְּרָסָה.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition> (of animals of prey) 
<italic>to attack with paws or claws</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ib. 53
<sup>a</sup>. Pes. 49
<sup>b</sup>; Snh. 90
<sup>b</sup>; a. fr.—Ḥull. III, 6 עוף הַדּוֹרֵס a bird of prey (that seizes food with its claws or eats animals before they are dead).—דְּרוּסָה f. 
<italic>an animal known to have been attacked by a beast or bird of prey</italic> (which are suspected of leaving a poisonous substance in the body). Ib. III, 1 (42
<sup>a</sup>) דְּרוּסַת הזאב an animal saved from the attack of a wolf.—יש דרוסה ל־ the case of a 
<italic>d’rusah</italic> applies to one attacked by &c. Ib. 52
<sup>b</sup>; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—4)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to stuff food into the camel’s mouth</italic>, contrad. to אָבַס a. הִלְעִיט.</definition>
<notes>—Sabb. XXIV, 3; Gen. R. s. 63; Num. R. s. 21.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Nif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נִדְרַס</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to be trodden down, to be effaced</italic> (by treading or otherwise).</definition>
<notes> B. Mets. 22
<sup>a</sup> עשוי לִידָּרֵס liable to be effaced; ib.
<sup>b</sup></notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<sense>

<entry id="D01118">
<head-word>דְּרַע, </head-word>

<head-word>(דְּרֹועָא) דְּרָעָא</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> c.
<language-key> ch. = h.</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="G00678">זְרֹועַ</xref></language-reference>, 
<italic>arm</italic>, (of animals) 
<italic>shoulder</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Ex. VI, 6. Targ. O. Num. VI, 19 (Y. אֶדְרֹועָא); a. fr.—Gitt. 31
<sup>b</sup>; Ber. 5
<sup>b</sup> לדְרָעֵיה, v. גְּלֵי. Keth. 65
<sup>a</sup> [read:] איגלי דְּרָעָהּ her arm was uncovered; a. fr.—[Gen. R. s. 80 שגלה בה דרועה, a corrupt., prob. to be read: שגלתה את זרועה.]—Yoma 33
<sup>b</sup> עבורי ד' וכ' it is forbidden to forego the arm in favor of the forehead, i.e. to reverse the order of putting on T’fillin (Deut. VI, 8; oth. interpret. v. Tosaf. a. l.). Ib. מד' (Ms. M. מאִידְרְעָא).—
<plural-form>Pl. דְּרָעַיָּא, דְּרֹועַ'</plural-form>. Targ. Ps. XXXVII, 17 דְּרֹועֵי.—
<pgbrk id="pg325" />Targ. O. Gen. XLIX, 24.—דְּרָעָתָא. Targ. Job XXII, 9 ודְרָעַת Ms. (ed. אדרעת).</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<head-word>דְּרָקֹון</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (δράκων) 
<italic>dragon, Boa Constrictor</italic> (v. Sm. Ant. s. v.).</definition>
<notes> [Its figure was used as a military ensign of the Roman cohorts. In Talm. it is considered an emblem of idolatry.] Ab. Zar. III, 3 if one finds vessels ועליהם … צורת ד' upon which is the figure of the sun … or of a dragon. Tosef. ib. V (VI), 2 איזהו מין ד' שאסור (v. ed. Zuck. note) what kind of serpent is forbidden (as an emblem of idolatry)?; Y. ib. III, 42
<sup>d</sup> top.—Lev. R. s. 16, beg. (ref. to תעכסנה, Is. III, 16; cmp. עָכִיס) שהיתה צורת ד' וכ' the figure of a serpent was on her shoes; Lam. R. to IV, 15 דרקין (corr. acc.). B. Bath. 16
<sup>b</sup>. Gitt. 56
<sup>b</sup> וד' כרוך עליה and a serpent wound around the barrel (allusion to the city of Jerusalem under the terrorism of the extremists). [Deut. R. s. 6 בא הדרבון, corr. acc.] [Y. Kil. I, 27
<sup>a</sup> bot. Ar., v. יַרְבּוּו.]</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="D01128">
<head-word>דְּרַרְיָא</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (an adaptation of διάῤῥοια, as if fr. דְּרֵי I; as to dialectic variations, v. infra) 
<italic>diarrhœa</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Lev. R. s. 18 (explain, זָרָא, Num. XI, 20) R. Ebiathar says, 
<italic>l’zara</italic> means לד' Ar.; Num. R. s. 7 לד' שאהיה נותן דורא וכ' (not אותן) Ar. (ed. לקרדא or לקדרא) it will cause diarhœa, for I will put a worm in their entrails. Sifré Deut. 1 דולריא; Pesik. Vattom., p. 131
<sup>a</sup> דרר' Ar. (Var. in Ar. a. ed. דלר', Ms. O. דרד', Ms. Parma דר אריא), v. גָּסָה. Gitt. 70
<sup>a</sup> (מלמטה) אוחזתו דל' will be seized with diarrhœa. [Ib. (מיושב) אוחזתו דל' ed., Ar. אלריא q. v.] Ib. מאי דל' (insert סם) what is the remedy for 
<italic>d</italic>.? Ans. דַּרְדָּרָא q. v.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="D01129">
<head-word>דָּרַשׁ</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (b. h.) </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to examine, question</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Denom. דְּרִישָׁה.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to expound, interpret</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ber. I, 5 עד שדְּרָשָׁהּ בן זומא until Ben Zoma found an intimation of it in the Biblical wording. Taan. 5
<sup>b</sup> מקרא אני דֹורֵשׁ I find it intimated in a Bible verse. B. Mets. 104
<sup>a</sup> היה ד' לשון הדיוט interpreted the popular (Chaldaic) wording used in documents. Pes. 22
<sup>b</sup>, v. אֵת; a. v. fr.—Part. pass. דָּרוּשׁ, f. דְּרוּשָׁה. Y. Yeb. VIII, 8
<sup>d</sup> top והלא ד' הוא has not the word ממנו been employed for interpretation?, opp. מופנה.—Denom. דְּרִישָׁה, מִדְרָשׁ.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition> (in gen.) 
<italic>to teach, lecture.</italic></definition>
<notes> Hag. II, 1 אין דֹּורְשִׁין ב־ you must not lecture on &c. Snh. 99
<sup>b</sup> ודורש בהגדות וכ' lectured on topics with the object of fault-finding; a. v. fr.—דֹּורֵשׁ 
<italic>lecturer</italic>. Ex. R. s. 42, beg. אבא הַדֹּ' Abba, the lecturer. Ib. s. 8, end, v. אֲמֹורָא.—
<plural-form>Pl. דֹּורְשִׁים</plural-form>. Snh. 38
<sup>b</sup>; Ab. Zar. 5
<sup>a</sup> דור דור ודֹורְשָׁיו every generation with its preachers. דֹּורְשֵׁי חמורות, v. חֹומֶר; ד' רשומות, v. רְשׁוּמָה. [M. Kat. II, 5 (13
<sup>b</sup>) דורשין Ms. M. (ed. עושין), read דֹּושְׁשִׁין.]</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Nif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נִדְרַשׁ</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to be interpreted, expounded</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Sifra, introd. rules שהתורה נִדְרֶשֶׁת בהן by which the Law is interpreted. Y. Peah II, 17
<sup>a</sup> דברים הַנִּדְרָשִׁין מן הכתב things which are derived by interpretation from the written code (Torah); הנדרשין מן הפה derived from the oral code (Mishnah). Y. Meg. I, 70
<sup>a</sup> top נתנה להִידָּרֵשׁ is a legitimate object of interpretation.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hithpa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִתְדָּרֵשׁ</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> same.</definition>
<notes> Y. Keth. III, 27
<sup>d</sup> top מִתְדָּרֵשׁ (מִתְדָּרְשָׁה) ולו וכ' the words 
<italic>v’lo</italic> &c. are open for interpretation, v. גְּזֵרָה.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="D01130">
<head-word>דְּרַשׁ</head-word>
<language-key> ch. </language-key>
<language-reference>same.</language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition />
<notes> [Targ. Jer. XLVIII, 26, some ed., ידרשון, v. דְּשַׁשׁ.] Targ. Jud. V, 9.—Succ. 51
<sup>b</sup> bot. קרא אשכחו ודָרוּשׁ they found a Bible verse and interpreted it. Arakh. 30
<sup>b</sup> איכא למִידְרְשִׁינְהוּ וכ' it may be interpreted in favor of a lenient practice &c.—Sot. 21
<sup>a</sup> דַּרְשַׁיה … להאי קרא R. … interpreted this verse. Ib. מאי דָרוּשׁ what verse did they interpret (to guide them in their action)?—Bets. 28
<sup>a</sup> דַּרְשִׁינָן משמך we taught in thy name. Yeb. 94
<sup>a</sup> הוה ליה … למִידְרַשׁ וכ' R. El. might have given a valuable interpretation &c., v. מַרְגְּנִיתָא. Lev. R. s. 9 עד דיחסל מִמִּדְרַשׁ until he ended his lecture. Ber. 28
<sup>a</sup> נִדְרֹושׁ מר וכ' shall this teacher lecture one Sabbath, and the other &c.? Ib. לִדְרֹושׁ ר' (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note); a. v. fr.—דָּרֵישׁ 
<italic>lecturer</italic>. Y. Yeb. XII, 13
<sup>a</sup> top ד' ודיין וכ' to serve as lecturer, judge &c.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Ithpe.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>אִידְּרִישׁ</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to be interpreted</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ber. 63
<sup>a</sup> האי קרא … מִדְּרִישׁ וכ' this verse (Ps. CXIX, 126) can be interpreted in its regular order (it is time to work &c., because people neglect the law) or in inverted order (the teachers ignore the letter of the law, because it is time to work for the Lord by guarding its spirit); ib. 60
<sup>a</sup>; Snh. 70
<sup>a</sup></notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<italic>here is a case speaking against you</italic>,] 
<italic>but, is’nt it?</italic> &c. Ib. 4

<sense>
<number>1)</number>

<sup>a</sup>.</definition>

<sup>b</sup>. Ber. 14
<sup>b</sup>; a. fr.—c) introducing

<entry id="E00028">
<head-word>הַבְדָּלָה</head-word>
<pos> f.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (בָּדַל) </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>cutting apart</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ḥull. 20
<sup>b</sup> מצות ה' the law ordering the separation of the head from the body (Lev. I, 15). Ib. ישנו בה' must be cut apart; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>separation</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 3 ויבדל ה' ממש 
<italic>vayyabdel</italic> (Gen. I, 4) means real separation (in space, not logical differentiation). Ḥag. 15
<sup>a</sup> ה' … דהואי the separation (of the waters) took place on the second day.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>Habdalah</italic>, a formula of prayer for the exit of the Sabbath or Festivals, v. 
<xref rid="A00042">אַבְדָּלָה</xref>.</definition>
<notes> Ber. VIII, 5; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. הַבְדָּלוֹת</plural-form>
<italic>the distinctions referred to in the Habdalah</italic>. Ḥull. 26
<sup>b</sup> bot.; Pes. 104
<sup>a</sup> סדר ה' the order of the subjects of distinction. Ib. מעין ה' האמורות וכ' corresponding to the distinctions mentioned in the Bible (Lev. X, 10 &c.).</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="E00029">

<senses>

<italic>to</italic>
<italic>glow;</italic> cmp. הבל) </definition>

<sup>a</sup>). Bets. 34
<sup>a</sup>. Sabb. II, 3 ולא הִבְהֲבָהּ and did not singe it (to prepare it for a wick).—Snh. 37
<sup>a</sup> is it possible for fire to be in contact with flax ואינה מְהַבְהֶבֶת and not to singe?—
<italic>Part. pass</italic>. מְהוּבְהָב 
<italic>lightly roasted</italic>. Y. ib. VIII, beg., 26
<sup>a</sup></notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to be like coals giving heat without flame; to nod consent without showing anxiety</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ber. 34
<sup>a</sup> שנים מהבהב (Y. ib. V, 9
<sup>c</sup> bot. מעמעם) if asked a second time, he must not consent &c.</notes></sense></senses>

<entry id="E00042">
<head-word>הֶבֶל</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>, constr.</definition>
<notes> הֲבֵל or הֲבַל (b. h.) </notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>breath, vapor, air, heat</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Sabb. 88
<sup>b</sup> בה' שבפיהם with the (fiery) breath of their mouths. Ib. 119
<sup>b</sup> ה' תינוקות וכ' the breath of school children. Ib. ה' שאין בו חטא a sinless breath (of children). Y. Ab. Zar. III, 42
<sup>d</sup> bot. ה' המרחץ וכ' the vapor of the bath room is injurious to the teeth. Yeb. 80
<sup>b</sup> אין בשרו מעלה ה' his body (after bathing) does not steam. Pesik. Baḥod. p. 154
<sup>a</sup>; Lev. R. s. 29 (ref. to Ps. LXII, 10) עד שהן עשויין ה' בתוך וכ' while they are yet a gas (in the first embryonic stage) …, they are predestined for marital union. Y. Ter. X, 47
<sup>a</sup> bot. הה' כובש the heat (of the fresh bread placed on top of an open wine casket) keeps the evaporations of the wine down. B. Kam. 50
<sup>b</sup> להַבְלוֹ for injuries suffered through the bad air of the pit (into which the animal fell), opp. to לחבטו injuries arising from knocking against the ground. Koh. R. to I, 2 ה' של תנור the hot air of the stove; ה' של עליונה the vapor of the topmost pot; Yalk. ib. 966 ה' שביעית; a. e.—
<pgbrk id="pg330" /></notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>2)</number>
<definition> (b. h.) 
<italic>vanity</italic>.</definition>
<notes> B. Bath. 16
<sup>b</sup> תנחומין של ה' vain consolations. Koh. R. l. c.; Yalk. l. c. (ref. to Ps. CXLIV, 4) לאיזו ה' to what kind of 
<italic>hebel</italic> (breath) man is like; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. הֲבָלִים</plural-form>. Ib. שבעה ה' וכ' the seven times that Solomon used the word 
<italic>hebel</italic>. Pesik. Baḥod. l. c.; Lev. R. l. c. כל ה' וכזבים וכ' all the vain things and falsehoods which the Israelites commit.</notes></sense></senses></entry>
